title: Majestic 12 committee

tellings.quote: rumored sort of committee around this in the UFO topic called the Majestic 12.

plain: Michels describes Majestic 12 as a secret committee that, allegedly, President Harry Truman formed in 1947 "to handle the extraterrestrial issue": an elite group of scientists, military and intelligence officials who advised the president directly on UFOs. He ties the scientist Vannevar Bush, a man named Gordon Gray, a scientist named Donald Menzel and General Nathan Twining to it, and elsewhere calls it only "rumored." He is retelling a disputed briefing paper for president-elect Dwight Eisenhower, dated 1952 and found anonymously on film in 1984. The paper says the group was "established by special classified executive order of President Truman on 24 September, 1947" and is "responsible directly and only to the President." The committee stands only as far as the paper does, and the paper's origin is in dispute: the FBI's copies are marked "BOGUS."

discussion.text: A typed briefing paper dated 18 November 1952, with a Truman memorandum to Secretary Forrestal of 24 September 1947 as its Attachment A, that came to light on a roll of 35mm film Jaime Shandera received anonymously at his Burbank home in 1984 and that he, William Moore and Stanton Friedman then studied; it was made public in 1987. The National Archives and the Truman and Eisenhower Libraries report their searches for it negative. The FBI's Majestic 12 file holds copies sent to it in 1988 and 1991, each marked "BOGUS" by hand, and records that the Air Force Office of Special Investigations "advised on November 30, 1988, that the document was fabricated" and that "the document is completely bogus". Philip Klass called the Truman memo an obvious fraud; Friedman judged the briefing paper and the memo "almost certainly genuine". The briefing paper says the operation is "responsible directly and only to the President of the United States" and is run by the "Majestic-12 (Majic-12) Group which was established by special classified executive order of President Truman on 24 September, 1947", and it lists twelve military, intelligence and scientific members. Michels retells the paper's own account, so the committee he describes stands as far as the paper does, and the paper's provenance is in dispute.
